prose: HiddenContent is an MCP server and API that checks documents for hidden text - content an AI agent would read but a human never sees - before the agent ingests it. The same capability ships as a browser extension for assistant-side checks and as an API for embedding in your own code, with one key covering both.

The onboarding is deliberately frictionless: sign up with GitHub (email only, no repo access), get a production key immediately with 20 free pages, then pay a cent per page with a $10 minimum via Stripe. Keys are stored as hashes and shown once; a device flow recovers lost keys. The pitch targets a real agent-security gap: invisible prompt-injection payloads riding inside otherwise normal pages and files.
highlights: Show HN: an MCP server that finds hidden text agents can read but humans cannot.
Two interfaces: a browser extension and an API, sharing one key and balance.
GitHub signup (email only); 20 free pages, then $0.01/page, $10 minimum.
Keys stored as hashes, shown exactly once; device-flow recovery.
Use case: screening documents for hidden injection content before an agent reads them.
